summary: Block. npm test passes 123 of 123, npm run check 11 of 11, tests/bash-prose.test.mjs 16 of 16. The a4-r3 delimiter fix holds, and the heredoc pass, which applies only when the whole call is plain file writes, showed no line the shell runs and the guard drops. I first suspected joinOpenPush runs before global options are stripped; that was wrong (line 124 strips them first, probes R1-R8 are denied). The loop repeats one pattern. Each round narrows a newline-spanning match to fit the criteria, checks the shell's own continuations, and misses another reader that rebuilds one command from several lines. This round: C-3 changed `git\s+push` to `git[ \t]+push`, so `git` ending one line and `push ...` on the next is no longer caught, though HEAD caught it because \s spans newlines. When xargs, tr or paste turns heredoc lines into arguments (`xargs <<EOF git` / `push origin main` / `EOF`), real bash 3.2.57 and zsh 5.9 push main, HEAD:main or --force in all eight cases. HEAD denied all eight; the worktree allows them in building and in done (F-1). This is the a4-r2 reviewer's F-2 class, fixed only for `git push` written together on the header line. Earlier findings were correct; none is disputed. The criteria are not contradictory: the patterns can match within one line after the guard joins lines a reader may rebuild, as joinOpenPush already does, so no human hold is needed. To stop the loop, apply the allow-list to the whole text: keep a newline as a boundary only between lines of plain words, and join from the first other line to the end.

findings.issue: The push deny pattern and push rule now require `git` and `push` on one line, and joinOpenPush joins lines only from a line holding `git push`, so a heredoc whose lines xargs, tr or paste rebuild into one command (`xargs <<EOF git` / `push origin main` / `EOF`, `tr '\n' ' ' <<'EOF' | bash` / `git` / `push origin main` / `EOF`) pushes main, HEAD:main or --force in building and in done, all of which HEAD denied.
findings.suggestion: Keep the allow-list approach but apply it to the whole text: in joinOpenPush, join every line from the first non-blank line that is not made of plain words (the WORD class, no quotes, `<`, `|`, `$`, backticks or parentheses) through the end of the text. The push line itself is not exempt from this rule. A plain push followed by plain or non-plain prose stays separate, so tests/bash-prose.test.mjs lines 401 to 406 still pass. Add X1 through X8 from /tmp/s1-a5-critic/probe2.mjs to the push test as denied cases.

/bin/bash 3.2.57(1)-release X1: stdout="git-arg[push] git-arg[origin] git-arg[goal/G-3] git-arg[main]"; X2: "git-arg[push] git-arg[--force] ..."; X5: "git-arg[push] git-arg[origin] git-arg[main]"; /bin/zsh 5.9 X1-X8 identical

findings.issue: A push line that is not bare `git push` plus plain words, such as the common `cd repo && git push origin goal/G-3`, is joined with every later line, so prose on the next line still counts as push arguments (`echo main is next` is denied), which is the failure C-3 targets, though in the fail-safe direction.
findings.suggestion: Optional: allow leading `cd WORD &&` segments in PLAIN_PUSH as PLAIN_WRITE already does.
